note: Canonical check registry . check_id is the join key: fragments -> dedup -> not_evaluated -> lint -> playbook -> category. stage names the pipeline stage the check guards (reach/read/extract/identify/trust/cite/land). pattern_template and evidence_template are the guardrail against incident-shaped findings : the title states the site- or template-level pattern, evidence carries the count with its denominator and quotes, affected_urls carries the instances. Fill placeholders from observations; never ship a title that names one specific visitor, session, or page as the pattern. negative_control is the when-NOT-to-flag a judge reads for. evidence_required values come from finding_fragment.json evidence_quality enum; semantic judgments stay capped at medium confidence unless a deterministic observation corroborates them. affected_surfaces_default uses only citation + live-fetch surfaces from provider_registry.json surface_taxonomy. Playbook prose (options, owners, acceptance-test templates, forbidden claims) lands in Phase 6 against these ids. Prefixes are exactly 3 letters per the schema pattern: ACC/REP/ANS/ENT/FRS/OFF/REF.

checks.pattern_template: Retrieval-crawler access to {page_class} pages is blocked by robots policy while browser traffic succeeds
checks.mechanism: A search-index crawler (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) disallowed on an important public page while a browser-UA fetch succeeds - OpenAI documents that sites disallowing OAI-SearchBot 'will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers'.
checks.evidence_template: robots.txt disallows {token} on {k} sampled {page_class} paths; the same paths return {browser_status} to a browser-UA fetch from the auditor's IP.
checks.negative_control: A training-bot-only disallow (GPTBot, ClaudeBot) is a policy choice, not a visibility outage - at most low, framed as policy; never a citation-loss finding.

checks.pattern_template: robots.txt is unavailable to crawlers ({http_status})
checks.mechanism: robots.txt returning 5xx can delay crawling; per severity_model rule 6, two or more consecutive 5xx across the audit is high/high, a single occurrence routes to needs_verification.
checks.evidence_template: {k} consecutive requests to /robots.txt returned {http_status}; a 404 would have meant 'no restrictions', which is not a defect.
checks.negative_control: robots.txt returning 404 means 'no crawl restrictions' - never a defect.

checks.pattern_template: {directive} on {page_class} pages removes them from {surface}
checks.mechanism: noindex / nosnippet / max-snippet:0 / data-nosnippet on an important public page - Google's AI-features doc names these as the controls limiting what AI Overviews / AI Mode can show.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} sampled {page_class} pages carry {directive} via robots meta or X-Robots-Tag ({urls}).
checks.negative_control: Intentional noindex on staging, duplicate, or internal URLs - verify intent before flagging; noindex on a page the site wants hidden is correct behavior.

checks.pattern_template: {page_class} pages carry {directive}, limiting Copilot's use of them
checks.mechanism: noarchive excludes a page from Bing Chat answers (not linked in answers); nocache limits it to URL/snippet/title - both documented by Bing while the page still ranks in ordinary results.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} {page_class} pages carry {directive} ({urls}); Bing documents the Copilot-answer effect for both directives.
checks.negative_control: noarchive on legal/archive pages carrying no decision facts - low or an opportunity, not a defect.

checks.pattern_template: Canonical signals conflict across {page_class} pages
checks.mechanism: Canonical declarations that disagree with redirect destinations, or conflicting canonicals, split retrieval-surface signals about the authoritative URL.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} sampled pages declare a canonical that disagrees with their redirect destination or with another page's canonical ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: Canonical pointing to the scheme/host-normalized self, or a deliberate single hop to the preferred host.

checks.pattern_template: Important URLs redirect through {hops}-hop chains or loops
checks.mechanism: Redirect loops or excessive chains prevent fetchers from reaching content at all.
checks.evidence_template: {k} sampled URLs required {hops}+ hops ({examples}); {loop_count} looped.
checks.negative_control: A single 301/308 hop to the canonical URL.

checks.pattern_template: Automated retrieval traffic receives a challenge where browser traffic succeeds
checks.mechanism: A bot challenge (WAF) served to retrieval-bot UAs but not browser UAs - distinguishable by differential status plus cf-mitigated headers and text/html content-type on non-HTML requests - blocks citation surfaces at the edge. Same-IP spoofed-UA evidence caps confidence at medium, so this check's practical severity ceiling is high (rule 1: critical requires high confidence).
checks.evidence_template: {token} UA received {bot_status} with {signal} where browser UA received {browser_status} on the same path; challenged responses were {content_type}. Observed from the auditor egress at audit time; edge behavior varies by visitor context.
checks.negative_control: Challenge triggered only on abusive paths or absent for robots-allowed tokens; a same-IP differential is suspected edge behavior, capped at medium confidence (severity_model).

checks.pattern_template: Important sitemap URLs are unreachable from sampled navigation
checks.mechanism: Important sitemap URLs unreachable from sampled navigation signal discovery structure problems on large or poorly linked sites.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} sampled sitemap URLs have no internal link from the sampled page set ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: A small, comprehensively linked site with no sitemap at all - Google documents sitemaps are not required there; never flag absence alone.

checks.pattern_template: The declared sitemap is {status}
checks.mechanism: A declared sitemap that 5xx's or fails to parse removes a discovery aid for index crawlers.
checks.evidence_template: {sitemap_url} returned {http_status}; parse_ok={parse_ok}.
checks.negative_control: Sitemap absent entirely on a small well-linked site (see ACC-SITEMAP-ORPHAN negative control).

checks.pattern_template: Locale alternates are missing or misdeclared on a multilingual site
checks.mechanism: On multilingual sites, missing or misdeclared locale alternates leave locale variants undiscoverable to region-sensitive retrieval.
checks.evidence_template: {k} locale variants found; {m} lack reciprocal hreflang declarations ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: Single-locale sites - the check is not applicable and lands in not_evaluated.

checks.pattern_template: A documentation-heavy site offers no llms.txt or Markdown alternates
checks.mechanism: Documentation-heavy sites without llms.txt or Markdown alternates miss a low-cost agent-navigation aid - an opportunity only, never discoverability.
checks.evidence_template: /llms.txt returned {http_status} on a docs-developer site with {n} sampled doc pages.
checks.negative_control: Any non-docs site, or any framing of llms.txt as a discoverability/ranking factor - Google states it does not use such files; 2026 studies found no citation effect.

checks.pattern_template: Key {fact_type} on {page_class} pages is absent from the raw server response
checks.mechanism: A key answer present after hydration or only in metadata is absent from raw visible text - non-rendering retrieval bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot measured; OAI-SearchBot third-party) read the raw response, so the fact is unretrievable there.
checks.evidence_template: Sampled {n} {page_class} pages; {k}/{n} omit {fact_type} from the raw response.
checks.negative_control: An SSR page whose #__next/__nuxt payload contains the same fact as visible raw text - must NOT flag; also not flaggable when the fact survives in an inline state payload (see REP-STATE-ONLY-FACT).

checks.pattern_template: {fact_type} appears only inside inline state payloads, not in visible text
checks.mechanism: A fact present only inside __NEXT_DATA__/RSC/Redux/Apollo payload strings and not in visible text is partially readable - AI crawlers may index initial-HTML JSON, so retrieval is degraded, not lost.
checks.evidence_template: {fact_type} found in {payload_key} on {k} pages but absent from visible text ({sample_count} sampled payload-only strings).
checks.negative_control: The fact also appears in visible raw text - pass, regardless of payload presence.

checks.pattern_template: {fact_type} is present in metadata but absent from the page's visible text
checks.mechanism: A fact present in og:description, meta description, or JSON-LD but absent from visible raw text yields inconsistent extractable claims across representations.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} pages state {fact_type} in {field} that never appears in their visible text ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: Metadata mirrors the visible text (normal description summarization is not a conflict).

checks.pattern_template: Main content on {page_class} pages is degraded or displaced in text extraction
checks.mechanism: The answer is lost, drowned in boilerplate, or fragmented by text extraction even though it exists in the DOM - readers and RAG pipelines extract worse than browsers render.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} {page_class} pages lose {content_type} under extraction; boilerplate-to-content ratio {ratio}.
checks.negative_control: Extraction preserves the answer sentence with its heading context.

checks.pattern_template: {fact_type} is carried only by {media_type} without text alternatives
checks.mechanism: Decision facts carried only by images with empty alt, canvas, SVG without text, or video without transcript are invisible to text extraction.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} {page_class} pages carry {fact_type} solely in {media_type}; {m} lack text equivalents.
checks.negative_control: A text alternative carrying the same fact is present and sufficient.

checks.pattern_template: Comparison data is laid out in non-semantic grids
checks.mechanism: Comparison grids built from aligned divs (>=3 columns, no <table>) lose row-column relationships under extraction - plan/price pairing can silently corrupt.
checks.evidence_template: {k} grids of >=3 aligned columns carry {content_type} with no <table> on the page.
checks.negative_control: A semantic <table> (or equivalent labeled structure) carries the same relationships.

checks.pattern_template: Section navigation on {page_class} pages requires script execution
checks.mechanism: Routes or destinations reachable only through script handlers (no crawlable <a href>) make sections undiscoverable to non-rendering fetchers.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} destinations are reachable only via script handlers; no crawlable <a href> equivalent exists ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: Crawlable same-origin <a href> links to the same destinations exist.

checks.pattern_template: Hidden text beyond accessibility patterns is present on {page_class} pages
checks.mechanism: Hidden text that is not an accessibility pattern (contrast to sr-only/skip-link allowlist) may indicate injected instructions or cloaking.
checks.evidence_template: {k} hidden-text instances across {n} pages after allowlisting sr-only/skip-link patterns ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: Legitimate sr-only, skip-link, or label patterns - allowlisted and never flagged.

checks.pattern_template: Category-standard questions about {topic} have no official answer on the site
checks.mechanism: An applicable archetype question (identity, capability, transaction, procedure, temporal, comparison, trust, local) has no official page or extractable answer on the site, so retrieval systems answer from third parties or skip the brand. Market-derived demand with no answering page feeds opportunities[], not findings.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} applicable archetype questions (source: {source_breakdown}) have no official answer page or extractable passage.
checks.negative_control: The archetype does not apply to this site type (site_type-gated) - do not force every archetype onto every site; unanswered market-derived topics are opportunities, not defects.

checks.pattern_template: Answers on {page_class} pages omit subject, units, or timeframe
checks.mechanism: The candidate answer passage lacks an explicit subject, units, or timeframe - extracted alone it under-informs or cannot be attributed.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} candidate answer passages omit {missing_element} ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: A complete, self-contained passage exists for the same question elsewhere on the page.

checks.pattern_template: Qualifications for {claim_type} claims are separated from the claim
checks.mechanism: The qualifier that makes a claim true (plan tier, region, exception) lives on a different page or behind interaction, so the claim extracted alone overstates what the site offers.
checks.evidence_template: {k} {claim_type} claims on {page_class} pages carry their qualifier elsewhere ({examples}: claim '{claim}' vs qualifier at {qualifier_location}).
checks.negative_control: The qualifier is attached to the claim in the same passage - the isolated-quote test passes.

checks.pattern_template: Comparison questions cannot be answered from the page's data layout
checks.mechanism: Comparison data laid out in non-semantic grids loses row-column relationships under extraction, so 'which plan includes X' or 'A vs B' questions extract as disconnected values. Judgment-side counterpart of REP-TABLE-SEMANTICS: pair them, do not double-report.
checks.evidence_template: {k} comparison questions ({examples}) map to grids whose plan-value pairing does not survive extraction.
checks.negative_control: The grid is semantic (see REP-TABLE-SEMANTICS pass) or the same comparison is available as extractable labeled text.

checks.pattern_template: Repeated boilerplate precedes or swamps main content in extraction
checks.mechanism: The answer is buried in or fragmented by boilerplate so that extraction yields navigation and legal text rather than the fact.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} pages open extraction with the same {boilerplate_chars}-char preamble; unique content starts at a median offset of {median_offset}.
checks.negative_control: The preamble is a few hundred characters of orientation and unique content starts early - quantified: median unique-content offset at or below ~1,500 characters (aligned with REP-EXTRACTION-LOSS's displacement bar) is a pass, with the measured numbers recorded as the non-evidence; the heading path still giving the extracted fragment enough context to survive on its own is also a pass; a broken sentence inside the preamble is an ANS-PASSAGE-INCOMPLETE fact, not this check.

checks.pattern_template: Structured data on {page_class} pages fails to parse or omits type-required properties
checks.mechanism: JSON-LD blocks that fail to parse or omit type-required properties deny systems a machine-readable entity description.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} JSON-LD blocks fail parsing; {m} omit type-required properties ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: Valid JSON-LD without @graph, or missing optional markup - never flagged; absence of a particular type is not invisibility.

checks.pattern_template: Structured data contradicts visible content on {fact_type}
checks.mechanism: Structured data contradicting visible content (price, availability, name) is worse than missing markup - it actively supplies a wrong quotable fact.
checks.evidence_template: {k} conflicts: schema says {schema_value}, page shows {visible_value} ({urls}).
checks.negative_control: Structured data matching visible claims, or clearly scoped to a different offer/page region.

checks.pattern_template: The organization name is stated {k} different ways across identity surfaces
checks.mechanism: The organization/product name varies across title, Open Graph, canonical, H1, JSON-LD, and footer, weakening entity resolution.
checks.evidence_template: title='{title_value}', OG='{og_value}', H1='{h1_value}', schema='{schema_value}', footer='{footer_value}' across {n} pages.
checks.negative_control: Intentional brand/product hierarchies with a consistent legal entity name.

checks.pattern_template: The brand name shares denotation with other prominent entities without distinguishing qualifiers
checks.mechanism: The brand name also denotes other prominent entities and the site provides no distinguishing category, location, or legal-name qualifier in title/H1/schema/about - the mistaken-identity risk from cross-web agreement.
checks.evidence_template: '{name}' also denotes {denotations}; homepage, title and Organization schema carry no {qualifier_type} that distinguishes the brand.
checks.negative_control: Distinguishing qualifiers are present in title, schema, and about-page - a shared name alone is never a finding.

checks.pattern_template: All declared external presence resolves to owned surfaces
checks.mechanism: None of the site's declared external-presence links resolve to independent (non-owned) corroboration surfaces, so claims rest entirely on the brand's own say-so.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} declared external links resolve; {independent_count} are independent; brand name matched on {match_count} destinations.
checks.negative_control: Independent surfaces exist and resolve with a matching brand name; owned social profiles (LinkedIn/X/Facebook) NEVER count as corroboration; timeouts never become findings.

checks.pattern_template: The site states different {claim_type} values for the same fact across pages
checks.mechanism: Pages on the same site state materially different values for the same fact (price, plan, version, hours) - the assistant will pick one, and misrepresentation follows.
checks.evidence_template: {claim_type}='{value_a}' on {url_a} vs '{value_b}' on {url_b} ({context_dates}).
checks.negative_control: Claims are consistent, or differences are intentional tier/regional variants clearly scoped on-page.

checks.pattern_template: Date signals disagree for {page_class} pages
checks.mechanism: Visible dates, structured dateModified, and sitemap lastmod disagree for the same page, undermining current-version identification.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} pages: visible {visible_date} vs structured {structured_date} vs sitemap lastmod {lastmod}.
checks.negative_control: Uniform sitemap lastmod without corroborating evidence of falsity is never auto-flagged; evergreen pages without dates are fine.

checks.pattern_template: Impossible or future dates appear on {page_class} pages
checks.mechanism: Future-dated or impossible dates signal untrustworthy freshness metadata to retrieval systems.
checks.evidence_template: {k} dates fall after audit time or are impossible ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: Extractor misreads (e.g. a version string or price parsed as a date) - verify semantic context before flagging.

checks.pattern_template: Sitemap lastmod values are uniform, indicating build stamps rather than content changes
checks.mechanism: A sitemap where every lastmod equals one build timestamp carries no per-page freshness signal and can misrepresent stale pages as current - a weak signal alone, escalated only with corroborating staleness evidence.
checks.evidence_template: {distinct}/{present} distinct lastmod values across {entries} entries; all sampled values are {sample_value}.
checks.negative_control: Varied lastmod values that track content, or a small sitemap where uniformity is plausible; never flag uniformity alone at medium or above.

checks.pattern_template: Superseded {artifact_type} remain linked and indexable without supersession signals
checks.mechanism: Current pages link into deprecated versions, or superseded product/policy pages stay indexable without supersession signals, so stale facts remain retrievable as current.
checks.evidence_template: {k} current pages link into deprecated {artifact_type}; {m} superseded pages lack forward signals ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: Intentional, clearly labeled historical/archive content.

checks.pattern_template: The brand is absent from answers to the inferred prompt set on {engine}
checks.mechanism: For prompts the site's own category implies, retrieval surfaces return answers without the brand - the demand exists and the site does not appear in it. One run is an observation, never a visibility score.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} recorded probes: engine={engine}, query='{query}', timestamp={timestamp}, brand absent. One run is one observation, auditor egress.
checks.negative_control: No search capability was declared, the prompt set is empty, or probes were shed at the deadline - the check is not_evaluated, never inferred from absence of evidence.

checks.pattern_template: Third-party sources are cited where the official page exists
checks.mechanism: Retrieval surfaces cite a third party (comparison site, directory, blog) instead of the brand's own page that answers the same question - the brand's voice is displaced in its own category.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} probes cite {third_party_domain} instead of {official_url} (engine={engine}, query='{query}', timestamp={timestamp}); one run is one observation, auditor egress.
checks.negative_control: No official page answers the question (that is ANS-QUESTION-UNANSWERED's cause, not this finding), or the third party is genuinely the better source for the prompt.

checks.pattern_template: Retrieval surfaces state the brand's {fact_type} incorrectly
checks.mechanism: The strongest case in the study: an answer states a fact about the brand that the brand's own page contradicts - misrepresentation the brand never wrote and cannot see.
checks.evidence_template: engine={engine} states '{stated_value}' for {fact_type} (query='{query}', timestamp={timestamp}); the official page states '{official_value}' at {official_url}; one run is one observation, auditor egress.
checks.negative_control: The stated value matches the official page, or the official page is genuinely ambiguous/absent on the fact - ambiguous source material is an ANS finding, not an OFF misrepresentation.

checks.pattern_template: Answers resolve the brand name to a different entity
checks.mechanism: The prompt resolves to a different entity sharing the name (place, person, category term), confirming the mistaken-identity risk that ENT-AMBIGUOUS-NAME detects the on-site side of. Pair the findings; do not double-report the cause.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} probes returned {other_entity_description} for the brand query (engine={engine}, query='{query}', timestamp={timestamp}); one run is one observation, auditor egress.
checks.negative_control: The probe output is unambiguous about the brand, or the ambiguity is already reported by ENT-AMBIGUOUS-NAME with its own evidence - report the on-site cause once and cite this as its observed effect.

checks.pattern_template: Nonexistent paths return {status} instead of 404
checks.mechanism: A nonexistent path returns 200 - a Google-recognized quality defect that admits junk URLs to indexes and turns mistyped/mangled AI citations into silent dead ends.
checks.evidence_template: Probe {probe_path} returned {status}; a correct 404/410 was expected. Observed from the auditor egress at audit time; edge behavior varies by visitor context.
checks.negative_control: Nonexistent paths return 404/410 with a useful body (see REF-404-DEAD-END for body quality).

checks.pattern_template: 404 responses offer no recovery path
checks.mechanism: A real 404 body offers no search, navigation, or suggestions - a visitor arriving from a stale or mangled AI citation has nowhere to go.
checks.evidence_template: The 404 body carries {body_signals} and lacks search, navigation, and suggestions. Observed from the auditor egress at audit time.
checks.negative_control: The 404 page provides search, navigation, or next-step suggestions.

checks.pattern_template: Non-canonical host/scheme variants drop the deep path
checks.mechanism: The http-to-https or www/apex variant redirects drop the path and dump the visitor on the homepage, so every citation of the non-canonical variant loses the answer entirely.
checks.evidence_template: {variant} redirect of {requested_path} lands on {final_path} instead of preserving the path. Observed from the auditor egress at audit time.
checks.negative_control: Variant redirects preserve the full path.

checks.pattern_template: Answer passages are not contiguous visible text runs
checks.mechanism: The cited passage is not one contiguous visible text run (price split across spans, claim assembled by script, passage inside a collapsed details element), so scroll-to-text-fragment landings fail silently.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} candidate passages are split across elements or absent from single blocks ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: The passage exists as a contiguous run and content headings carry stable ids.

checks.pattern_template: The landing answer for {intent} is not confirmable above the fold
checks.mechanism: The visitor arrives with a pre-formed question; the expected answer is not confirmable in the first screenful of main content with its qualifier attached, so the referral bounces.
checks.evidence_template: {k}/{n} questions: answer absent from the first screenful or qualifier detached ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: The answer appears above the fold with its qualifier - a slogan H1 with the fact 900 words down is the flag case, not the pass case.

checks.pattern_template: Landing answers are collapsed by default on {page_class} pages
checks.mechanism: The landing answer is in the DOM but collapsed by default - fine for the machine, hostile to the human who arrived for exactly that fact (the accordion inversion: click-injected counterparts belong to REP-KEY-FACT-LOSS).
checks.evidence_template: {k} decision facts live inside collapsed-by-default containers ({tag_types}) on {page_class} pages.
checks.negative_control: The answer content is visible on arrival (expand-on-demand is fine for supplementary content).

checks.pattern_template: Overlays block main content in the initial response
checks.mechanism: A consent, paywall, login, or interstitial overlay present in the initial HTML blocks the cited answer on arrival.
checks.evidence_template: {overlay_type} present in raw HTML on {k}/{n} sampled pages ({examples}).
checks.negative_control: A dismissible banner that does not obstruct main content, or overlays required by law on the specific content class.

checks.pattern_template: Static indicators suggest slow landings on {page_class} pages
checks.mechanism: Static risk indicators (undimensioned media, render-blocking scripts) suggest a slow landing - recorded as a performance-risk observation or needs_verification hypothesis, NEVER as a measured Core Web Vital.
checks.evidence_template: {k} undimensioned media, {m} render-blocking scripts on {n} {page_class} pages (risk observation only; no synthesized CWV).
checks.negative_control: No fabricated CLS/LCP/INP numbers, ever; real measurement requires field data (CrUX) or a lab run, which the audit does not perform.

checks.pattern_template: Sampled internal links return errors
checks.mechanism: Internal links that 404 or 5xx strand visitors and crawlers on error pages; link equity and citation paths die with them. 410 Gone is correct removal, not rot.
checks.evidence_template: {k} of {n} sampled internal links return {statuses} ({examples}); sample probes unfetched same-origin links only.
checks.negative_control: 410 Gone responses (correct removal); timeouts, which never become findings; external links (a separate concern); a sample with zero errors.
